meta.title: Use GitHub App installation tokens for projection writes
meta.author: Codex manager

feature.problem_statement: ProjectV2 projection writes still use a long-lived ORCHESTRATOR_GITHUB_TOKEN even though the repository already persists board/source installations and has a cached GitHub App installation-token provider.
goals: Resolve each target project to its persisted board-owner installation and use a short-lived App installation token for ProjectV2 writes.
Remove static projection-token configuration and Secret/Helm/documentation plumbing without leaving a fallback path.
Refresh expired tokens and retry authentication/rate-limit failures in a bounded, context-aware, secret-safe way.
Preserve durable receipt semantics so failed projections remain replayable and idempotent.
non_goals: Redesigning observer source-installation data or adding OAuth/user-token flows
Replacing the existing durable receipt/outbox model with a new queue
Changing GitHub project field semantics or host event APIs
Publishing credentials or relying on static-token compatibility
scope_in: Installation-token provider/client and GraphQL write retry behavior
Server projector wiring and persisted board-owner installation resolution
Static token removal from config, dev values, rendered Secret references, docs, and tests
Unit/integration tests and minimum App permission documentation
scope_out: External Vault/ESO provisioning and live App permission changes
Production rollout and authenticated DEV write readback
New durable projection scheduler beyond existing receipt replay

requirements.statement: ProjectV2 projection writes must resolve the target project’s persisted board-owner installation and fail closed on missing or ambiguous ownership; source-owner installations remain observer/enrichment credentials.
requirements.rationale: A write must use the installation that owns the board, not a global token or an arbitrary source-owner fallback.

requirements.statement: The projection client must obtain short-lived installation tokens through the existing provider, request/validate a minimum permission map, and have no static token or fallback constructor path.
requirements.rationale: Long-lived projection credentials increase blast radius and violate the App-auth contract.

requirements.statement: Provider/client auth failures must invalidate and force one token refresh on expiry/401, retry rate-limit responses with bounded context-aware backoff honoring retry hints, and never retry ordinary permission denials indefinitely.
requirements.rationale: Short-lived tokens and GitHub rate limits are normal; retries must be safe, bounded, and observable without leaking secrets.

requirements.statement: Projection receipts remain unprojected until the complete convergent write succeeds, and a failed or lost response can be replayed idempotently without duplicate work-item/timeline effects.
requirements.rationale: Replacing credentials must not lose host projection intent.

requirements.statement: ORCHESTRATOR_GITHUB_TOKEN, github-token Secret references, GitHubToken fields, and separate static projection-token documentation must be removed from runtime config, Helm/dev values, tests, and operator docs.
requirements.rationale: Leaving the old contract mounted would preserve the credential risk and make rollout ambiguous.

requirements.statement: Documentation must state the minimum App permissions for board ProjectV2 writes and observer/source enrichment, and identify the required live DEV/App verification without recording token values.
requirements.rationale: Operators need an auditable permission and rollout contract.

requirements.statement: Focused tests must cover provider refresh/cache isolation, permission request validation, 401 rotation, 429/GraphQL rate limits, mixed-owner selection, replay durability, and static-token absence.
requirements.rationale: The security-sensitive behavior must be regression-tested locally before live validation.

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Given a project with a persisted board-owner installation and mixed source owners, when a field projection is written, then the client requests a token for the board-owner installation and no static token path is reachable.

Given an expired or unauthorized cached token, when GraphQL returns an authentication failure, then the provider invalidates that installation cache, obtains one fresh token, retries once, and returns a sanitized bounded error if it still fails.

Given a 429 or explicit GraphQL rate-limit response with a retry hint, when projection executes, then it waits only within the configured/context deadline and retries a bounded number of times; ordinary permission denial is not looped.

Given a projection mutation succeeds but receipt marking is interrupted, when the same durable host/dispatch event is replayed, then the write converges idempotently and the receipt becomes projected without duplicate timeline/work-item rows.

Given the rendered DEV deployment and repository search, when static credential removal is checked, then no ORCHESTRATOR_GITHUB_TOKEN, github-token key, GitHubToken field, or static projection-token documentation remains and the App permission matrix is documented.

Given the candidate commit, when focused tests, race/full Go validation, Helm/docs/static scans, and hosted checks run, then they pass; issue closure additionally requires sanitized live App write/readback evidence.

test_plan.approach: Use httptest/fakes and a controllable clock to verify per-installation token cache, minimum permission request/validation, forced refresh after 401, bounded 429/GraphQL rate-limit retry, and sanitized errors.
Exercise server projector with persisted board/source installations and durable host/dispatch receipts; assert board-owner selection and replay/idempotency after projection/marking failure.
Run repository grep, rendered Helm/dev deployment checks, docs checker, and configuration contract tests proving static token absence and documented permissions.
Run focused packages, race tests, go vet, full make ci, OpenAPI/Helm/workflow checks, and exact-head hosted validate.
Use an approved DEV App installation to perform one sanitized protected board projection/readback with App-only credentials and verify pod/runtime Secret keys; do not record tokens.

review_checks: Board-owner resolver is explicit and unknown/ambiguous ownership fails closed
validation_checks: Sanitized DEV write/readback uses expected installation

review_checks: No static token field/env/constructor fallback; permission map is bounded
validation_checks: Rendered deployment has App credentials only

review_checks: Retries are bounded, context-aware, and distinguish permission denial
validation_checks: Focused retry suite and sanitized live status evidence

review_checks: Receipt remains unprojected until confirmed; replay is idempotent

validation_checks: Helm/dev rendered deployment and runtime key names

review_checks: Permission matrix names board write and source read responsibilities
Focused and full validation coverage is present
validation_checks: Hosted validate and clean worktree/resource evidence

perspectives.summary: Provider injection, board-owner resolution, forced refresh, and bounded retries are the core runtime change.
Fail closed on ownership ambiguity, permission escalation, and static-token remnants; do not leak secrets.
Cover provider/HTTP/replay fixtures and require sanitized live App write evidence before closure.
Keep observer/data model stable and separate external rollout from repository implementation.

council.consensus_summary: Implement board-owner installation-token projection with no static fallback, explicit permissions, bounded retry, durable replay tests, and honest live validation gates.
open_questions: What exact minimum permission map is currently granted to the installed App for organization/repository Projects writes?
Does the live target project always have one persisted board-owner installation, and how should a missing/ambiguous association be repaired?
Can DEV protected write/readback be run after rollout without exposing credentials?
